chapter: Guitarists and the Pierron and Brown bands
title: Why Souchon prefers banjo to guitar in a band
summary: He would rather play banjo with a band because it kicks the rhythm along and cannot be turned off the microphone. The old guitar could be heard only near the band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You're asking about the difference between banjo and guitar, which you really prefer and which most of the musicians here prefer. Why did the style change from one to the other?

Well, I personally rather play a banjo with a band. I think it kicks it along much better and they can't turn that damn microphone off like they do when I play a guitar. They can't hear me a damn bit and they're forced to hear me with a banjo. But personally, not only about myself, I think a banjo does kick a band along.
In the real old days, say back in the 1910 period, could you really hear that guitar? Because half the time you can't hear it.

You could if you were up close to the band, but I mean, having no microphones or anything like that, it just, I think it was for the band itself, the solid cording and the solid rhythm that they used, it helped the band itself more than it did the dancers. I think, of course, that the pieces like the blues had no business to be played on the banjo at all. Now, one of the things that I was going to completely overlook was the fact that we danced by Brown's band many times. Oh, yeah. And I followed, I used to go to the prize fights, I was quite a fan even as a kid, and that's why I was fortunate enough to hear both Happy Shilling and Brown's band and the third one, what's his name, Johnny Fisher.
